title: Performance Investigation
prompt:
Profile a deliberately slow synthetic endpoint, measure baseline latency and database query counts, remove a demonstrated bottleneck, and compare repeated before/after measurements.

Submission: provide the implementation or design, a relevant test, expected outputs, one failure/boundary case, and version/runtime notes. Flask server code is not executed inside the CodeLeaf browser preview; local verification or human review is required.

starter.content:
from time import perf_counter

start = perf_counter()
# Run a representative workload here.
elapsed_ms = (perf_counter() - start) * 1000

expected_output: A report documents the workload, environment, baseline distribution, bottleneck evidence, change, and repeat measurements.
acceptance_criteria: A report documents the workload, environment, baseline distribution, bottleneck evidence, change, and repeat measurements.
Document setup/run steps and mark whether verification was static, local, or human-reviewed.
Do not include private credentials or use real personal data.
Include a negative/boundary case and explain the expected status/result.
hints: Use the same data and workload before and after the change.
Do not rely on one noisy measurement or introduce caching without invalidation rules.
grading_method: Static required-string smoke check plus human review of implementation correctness, tests, validation/security boundaries and reproducibility. The platform does not execute arbitrary Python/Flask code.
retry_policy: Retries are allowed after reviewing feedback; the platform backend controls its uniform reward and idempotency rules.
status_note: Practice assignment mapped to the supplied Flask PDF. Needs subject-matter review before publication.
